(iii) Social value
Social values of biodiversity refers to the manner in
which the bio-resources are used to the society.

* These are the values associated with the social life,
religion and spiritual aspects of the people.

* Holy plants: Many of the plants are considered holy
plants in our country like Tu/si, Mango, Lotus, Neem etc.

* Holy animals : Many of the plants are considered holy
animals in our country like cow, snake, peacock etc.,
(iv) Ethical value
Ethical and moral value is based on the importance of protecting all forms of life.
It involves ethical issues like ‘’ All life must be preserved’’

The ethical value means that a species may or may not be used, but its existence in
our nature gives us pleasure.

Ex: 1. The river Ganga is considered as holy river.
2. Vembu, Tulsi are some of the trees worshipped by the Tamilans.

3. We are not deriving anything from Kangaroo, Zebra, but we feel that these should
exist in nature.

(v) Aesthetic value
The beautiful nature of plants & animals insist us to protect the biodiversity.

Ex: People from far and wide spend a lot of time and money to visit beautiful areas
where they can enjoy the aesthetic value of biodiversity and this type of tourism is
now known as ecotourism.

The pleasant music of world birds, colour of flowers, peacock, and butterfly are
important aesthetic value.

(vi) Option value

It includes the potential of biodiversity that are presently unknown and need to be
explored. The optional values of biodiversity suggest that any species may be proved
to be a valuable after someday. (i.e., presently unknown but need to be known)

Eg., growing Biotechnology field is searching a species which can cure diseases like
cancer and AIDS.

b) What are alternative energy resources? How it fulfill the future energy
need.

Ans. The energy resources that can be regenerated easily through natural process once
they are used up are called the renewable or alternative energy resources.

Renewable energy resources include solar energy, wind power, hydropower etc.

As the conventional fossil fuel energies like coal, petroleum, natural gas and nuclear
energy are not abundant and one day will be exhausted, so we should depend more on
the alternative non-conventional energy resources. The advantages of alternative
energies are

(i) They are plenty in sources
(i) Non-polluting and eco-friendly
These types of energy can fulfill our future energy demand.
‘Various types of alternative energy resources are
e Solar energy
e = Wind
